Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Atmaram Singh
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Atmaram Singh learned counsel for the respondent as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the entire record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 22.12.2022 passed by the Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Allahabad.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that in this case he is innocent and has committed no offence with the victim as stated in F.I.R. for commission of rape and the victim Ravindra @ Ravidra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195985034/
1 becoming conceived.

entities.text: Ravindra @ Ravidra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also submitted that the victim gave birth to a child regarding which D.N.A.
was also done and F.S.L. report has also been called for by this Court.

The prosecution was directed to collect D.N.A. report which has been provided by learned A.G.A. which is on record and shows that the appellant is not a biological father of a child though victim is biological mother which shows that the appellant did not establish physical relations with the victim but the allegation in this regard was false.
The appellant is on interim bail and has not misused the liberty granted by this Court, therefore request to enlarge him on regular bail.
It is further submitted that the appellant is languishing in jail since 25.11.2022 having no any criminal antecedent.
Learned counsel for the appellant also referred to the amended provisions of SC/ST Act.

All these facts were not taken into consideration by the learned Special Judge while rejecting the bail which cannot be said to be lawful,
therefore requested to set it aside and allow the appeal.
Learned counsel for the respondent as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid but could not dispute the the contents of D.N.A. report.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, the D.N.A. report, it appears that the learned Special Judge has not taken into consideration all these facts while considering bail, therefore, the order passed by learned court below cannot be said to be lawful and is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant Ravindra @ Ravidra Singh involved in Case Crime No. 187 of 2022 under Sections 376, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3(2)(V) SC/ST Act, Police Station Manda, District Prayagraj be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
